proposals.evidence: DEDR1173 gives Kota gaṇḍ male (Kannada gaṇḍu), and4616 gives Kota mog child with Kannada maga/magu and Tulu mage son. LSI ganḍu mage Son is transparently male + child: preserve the survey dental n spelling, vowels and word order, and represent both components rather than assigning the entire response to one stem.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4395(a) gives Kota peṇ female (compare Kannada peṇṇu), and4616 gives Kota mog child, with Kannada maga/magu and Tulu mage. LSI peṇṇe mage is female + child; the identical singular and plural elicitation responses remain distinct records without inventing a plural ending. The Badaga annotation in4395 applies to eṇ, not to the separate peṇ entry.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1711(a) gives Kota kudyr horse, with Kannada kudire/kudure/kudare and Kodagu kudïre. Both LSI horse responses fit this article family; the male and plural elicitation labels and differing medial vowels remain unchanged. Similarity to Kannada alone does not establish an immediate donor.
